title: autotrade — discovery: find a strategy for a new trade
_why: Run this when starting a new trade, not on a schedule. Discovery searches broadly for a rule
that does not exist yet; revising one that already runs is a different job with a different
search space, and doing both every night produces a new stranger each morning while the
running rules never improve. revise.example.json is the nightly one.
The sequence is fixed rather than left to an agent turn, because a run that re-authors its own
steps is a run whose steps can be wrong every time, and this one writes what will trade.
Step 2 is the model's whole contribution: where in parameter space to look. Steps 3-6 measure.
Step 7 adopts, receiving the ranking, the planned runs and their results as they came out of
those steps — so the evidence never passes through the model.

pipeline.instruction:
You are given today's strategy review and the history of what has already been adopted or refused. Answer with a JSON object only — no prose, no explanation — describing where to search next for a trading rule.

Shape:
{"families":[...],"fast":[...],"slow":[...],"low":[...],"high":[...],"stopLossPct":[...],"takeProfitPct":[...],"holdout":0.3}

families is any of: ma-cross, ema-cross, rsi, bollinger, macd. The numeric fields are lists of parameter values to try; null is allowed in stopLossPct and takeProfitPct to mean "no stop". holdout is the fraction of history kept back for scoring.

Read the refusals in the history. A combination that was refused for too few trades will be refused again at the same parameters, so move somewhere else: slower parameters trade less, faster ones trade more. Keep the space under about 200 combinations — a wider search finds a better-looking result without finding a better rule.

whatTheModelCannotDo: Turn trading on, set the mode, arm real money, raise a limit, or write a result.
It proposes a region of parameter space. Everything that decides whether that region
produced something tradable is machine output flowing between steps.
universe: The symbols, the confirmation set, the broker and the account come from the module settings —
they are the owner's walls, not part of a schedule. Only the candle loop still names them here,
because a FOREACH needs its list up front; keep it in step with the `universe` setting.
